chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Safwan and Ibn Abi Umayr from Rifa'ah ibn Musa said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who vowed to walk to the House of Allah (al-Haram), so he walked; will it suffice him for the Hajj of Islam? He said, 'Yes.'
ai.seo_question: Does walking to Mecca to fulfill a vow count as the obligatory Hajj?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), recorded in al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, the validity of fulfilling the obligatory Hajj through a voluntary vow (nadhr) to walk to the Kaaba is confirmed. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that a specific vow can substitute for the general obligation, provided the act is completed with the intention of fulfilling the duty. It underscores the flexibility within Shia fiqh regarding the mode of performing Hajj when bound by a personal vow.
